**Video Killed the Radio Star.** For a whole day the T-Deck's screen and its LoRa radio fought over the same three wires, and every time the radio spoke, the picture tore, froze, or fell over. The screen was winning. Then they agreed to share: same wires, same settings, the radio speaks between frames, and nobody gets hurt. Video did not, in the end, kill the radio star. They're roommates now. Also, a meatball moved into the snow.

<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skizzophrenic/SquachWatch-CYD/v1.37.0/docs/video-killed-the-radio-star.gif" width="480" alt="Squachy on the snowy SNOWFALL background with a small igloo crossing the slope behind him. Then a round, rust-brown meatball with a lumpy edge, two stray hairs and a sleepy face sits beside Squachy. He eats a catch on a night city background, stretches into a hot dog saying Look! A hot dog!, gets thrown and splits into three little meatballs saying Everybody roll back! Meet in the middle!, and finally turns into an igloo saying I'm a igloo now. Nobody's home."></p>

**Meet M3@ty.** Somebody lives in the igloo that slides across SNOWFALL. You can see two eyes in the door. Knock three times (as slowly as you like, it's an easy one) and out rolls M3@ty: a meatball. He's helping. You just can't tell yet. His face stays perfectly still while the rest of him rolls, which he is very proud of. He eats every catch Squachy makes (a little morsel in the catch's colour drops in and he swells up), and if the catch was a serious one he hides as an igloo for a bit. Now and then he shows you a hot dog. He can do a hot dog every time. When Squachy dances he does "Shake it!". Throw him and he splats; throw him HARD and there are three of him, who then roll back together and meet in the middle. He has about a hundred things to say and says one every 20 to 40 seconds, so he will not run out soon. Squachy has opinions about him eating the evidence.

**The T-Deck talks LoRa.** Last release the T-Deck's radio sat this one out because it shares its wiring with the screen and the two couldn't take turns without the picture paying for it. They can now. The radio stopped being a stranger on the bus and started sending its bytes through the screen's own path, between frames, at its own speed, and then hands everything back exactly how it found it. It listens to Meshtastic and MeshCore just like the T-Watch: the pink LORA n NEW pill on the main screen, LORA CHATS with a tab for each network, and a ding when something new comes in. One honest note: with BOTH networks on, the T-Deck has to take turns between them, and MeshCore only announces a message for 65 ms, so in BOTH it catches most Meshtastic messages but only about one MeshCore message in four. If MeshCore is your thing, pick MESHCORE.

**And it sends.** It has a keyboard, so it would be rude not to. Turn on LORA TX in Settings (it starts OFF; then 10 or 20 dBm, and never more than 14 in the EU band), open LORA CHATS, type, press Enter. Your message goes out on the open tab's network: Meshtastic's public LongFast channel, or MeshCore's Public channel under your squad nickname. It shows up in the chat as YOU. These are public channels, so anyone nearby with a Meshtastic or MeshCore radio can read it, and anyone can type any name on them. Please be nice. Squachy is listening. Squachy is always listening.

**CROWD NONE.** With a desk full of SquachWatches, every one of them kept wandering onto every other one's screen to visit. Fun, until you're trying to test something. CROWD now has a NONE setting: nobody visits, nobody crowds, every board keeps its own Squachy to itself, and the squad count, messages and heads-ups all still work.

**A bigger lava lamp on the watches.** The battery lamp on the T-Watch sits right against the left edge now, and one and a half times the size. You can read it from across the room. If your room is small.

**Under the hood.** The pets that can be thrown (C1iPPY, T0@$TY, the yeti and M3@ty) used to carry a copy each of the same flight maths. Now they share one, and every throw still lands exactly where it did (we filmed 560 frames of it to check). M3@ty himself went on a diet before the release: his body, his face and his lines got packed down from 18.5 KB to 14.4, and he looks and talks exactly the same.

### The actually-useful part

**Added**
- M3@ty, a new pet: knock three times on the igloo on SNOWFALL. Eats catches, hides as an igloo after serious ones, does a hot dog, dances along with Squachy, splats when thrown and splits in three on a hard landing. About a hundred lines, one every 20 to 40 seconds.
- LoRa on the LilyGo T-Deck Plus: Meshtastic and MeshCore listening with the LORA n NEW pill, LORA CHATS and a ding, set in Settings > SYSTEM > LORA.
- Sending from the T-Deck: LORA TX in Settings (OFF, 10 dBm, 20 dBm; 14 dBm at most in the EU band) and a compose line in LORA CHATS. Enter sends on the open tab's network.
- CROWD NONE: no visits and no crowd on the main screen; the squad badge, messages and heads-ups carry on.
- Console: `MEATY` (unlock him), `MEATY IGLOO | DOG | SHAKE | SPLIT`, `MEATY LOCK` (earn him again).

**Changed**
- The T-Watch's battery lamp sits against the left edge at one and a half times the size.
- The throwable pets share one flight path; M3@ty is about 4 KB smaller than when he was first built.
- On the T-Deck, the counter tiles drop under the LORA pill only while it is showing.
- BACK from LORA CHATS goes straight to the main screen, on the watches and the T-Deck.
